title: Combination Sum
source: canonical Combination Sum concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of distinct positive integers and a target. Return every combination of values that sums exactly to target, where a value may be used any number of times. Combinations that differ only in order count once. Sort the values inside each combination ascending, and sort the list of combinations ascending.

examples.explanation: 3 + 5 and 4 + 4 are the only ways to reach 8.
Twos alone never land on an odd target.

hints: Reuse means a recursion that stays on the same value is allowed; skipping forward past it is what keeps combinations unique.
Feed the recursion a start index: candidate values before it may not be picked again, which kills reordered duplicates.
When the remainder hits zero, record a copy of the picks; when a candidate overshoots the remainder, abandon that branch.
solution: Backtracking over a start index: each step tries candidates from the index onward (reuse allowed by retrying the same index), pruning the moment a value overshoots. Sorting first lets the pruning break early. Output normalized by sorting. Exponential in the target, with O(target) recursion depth.
failureHint: hidden tests include impossible targets and targets reachable only by reusing values

visible.failNote: values may repeat inside one combination
an unreachable target returns an empty list
